approved_findings: The November 7 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/advanced/dashboard-payment-methods is a 14-line variant index (new lines 5-14) linking Checkout Sessions embedded-components and Payment Intents elements pages. The April 21 capture bundled full versions of both paths (old lines 8-327). The apparent removal in the diff is a rendering or capture-structure change; it does not establish changed payment-method behavior or deprecation. Neither linked variant body is pinned in this unit.

The dated old guide says removing payment_method_types migrates preferences to Dashboard management for existing Checkout Sessions and Payment Intents integrations (old lines 18-20 and 227-229). Non-default methods such as bank redirects are initially disabled on upgrade and must be re-enabled in Dashboard. Current source lines 13 and 17-19 retain this main split and warning; keep them tied to the April capture rather than treating the November index as renewed behavioral proof.

Current source lines 29-30 frame nine delayed-notification methods as requiring additional webhook handling. The old Checkout section says the step is only required if the integration plans to use listed methods (old line 64), and its preceding paragraph conditions a webhook update on automatic fulfillment and adding a first delayed method (old lines 60-62). Correct the source to preserve those conditions rather than implying every migration requires those webhooks.

Current source line 37 labels checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded as 'Funds cleared'. The old event table says the customer payment succeeded and recommends fulfilling the purchase (old line 73); it does not assert balance availability or settlement. Correct the event description to 'Payment succeeded' while preserving the source's paid-status check on checkout.session.completed (old lines 72-74, 125-156).

The old Payment Intents variant recommends payment_intent.succeeded and, for delayed methods, payment_intent.payment_failed (old lines 259-263). Current source lines 40-45 correctly distinguish that event family from Checkout Session events. The source's April raw_files pointer should remain the factual evidence; the November index is navigation-only.
approved_conflicts: Source lines 29-30 overstate a conditional delayed-notification integration step as a blanket requirement, compared with old lines 60-64.

Source line 37's 'Funds cleared' is stronger than old line 73's 'payment succeeded' and can misstate settlement or balance availability; old line 66 explicitly warns that delayed-method funds are not immediately available.
historical_claims_to_preserve: April 21 guide: the migration instruction to remove payment_method_types applies to existing Checkout Sessions and Payment Intents paths separately, and previously configured non-default methods may need Dashboard re-enablement (old lines 18-20, 227-229).
April 21 guide: Apple Pay enabled and Google Pay disabled by default in the described setup; automatic tax without shipping address can hide Google Pay even when enabled (old lines 48-50, 247-249).

April 21 guide: delayed-payment handling is conditional on the merchant using listed methods and on the fulfillment integration; Checkout completed can indicate authorization while payment_status is unpaid, with async success or failure later, whereas Payment Intents uses its own succeeded/payment_failed events (old lines 60-74, 125-156, 259-263).
April 21 test cards and bank details in source lines 47-65 are test-mode examples, not production payment guarantees (old lines 174-215 and 286-327).
unresolved_questions: The November variant links at new lines 13-14 were not captured as detailed pages in this pinned job, so their current settings, eligibility, event guidance, and any changes after April are unverified.
